source_review.notes: Checked all six references at OWASP, the RFC Editor, or MITRE. OWASP API1:2023 covers identifier-driven object enumeration and per-object checks; API3:2023 covers excessive property exposure and explicit minimal projection. Current Authentication and Forgot Password cheat sheets confirm generic messages and approximately uniform processing for account existence cases. RFC 9110 permits 404 concealment of forbidden resources. Current CWE 4.20 defines observable discrepancy as unauthorized differentiation correlated with internal/security state.

evidence: Reviewed protected fact Z, transcript tau, conditional distribution L(tau|Z=z), authorized object set O_c, client query Q, and contract/read/purpose field sets for consistent definitions.
Confirmed direct, differential, inferential, and amplified disclosure are distinguished and all TeX uses GitHub-compatible delimiters.
Confirmed approximate distribution equivalence is explicitly an engineering objective under a stated observer/query model rather than exact equality.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The notation separates direct object/property projection guarantees from broader transcript distinguishability.

numerical_recomputation.notes: No measured latency distribution, statistical effect, privacy budget, entropy threshold, or quantitative benchmark is claimed. Example milliseconds/counts are hypothetical traces requiring production measurement.

evidence: Re-derived returned objects as Q intersection O_c, confirming client filters cannot widen the authorized set.
Re-derived F_out as contract intersection readable intersection purpose fields, confirming every returned property must satisfy all three bounds.
Checked that matching L(tau|Z=z0) and L(tau|Z=z1) is intentionally stronger than matching status/body and remains approximate under real system noise.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter explicitly states row/field subset safety does not imply safety of counts, timing, order, lengths, caches, errors, or query composition.

evidence: Reviewed absent/forbidden/private/public objects; known/unknown/locked/disabled accounts; login/signup/invite/reset/email lookup; IDs/slugs/cursors; and authorized versus unauthorized existence knowledge.

Reviewed fields/null/shape, nested relationships, lists/counts/facets/search/order/cursors/aggregates/exports, GraphQL aliases/errors/subscriptions, batches, alternative formats, HEAD/conditional/range, and legacy/debug/support paths.

Reviewed cold/warm CDN/cache, ETag/length/compression, redirects/cookies/connections, rate-limit buckets/headers, email/SMS/webhook/owner notifications, logs/traces/metrics/analytics, repeated timing, differencing, prefix/ID walking, concurrent/distributed probing, and public scraping.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial review covers direct values, differential channels, compositional inference, infrastructure leakage, and automation amplification.

evidence: Executed minimal-equivalent-responses: known and unknown reset requests returned identical 202/message pairs; peer-forbidden and absent private profiles returned identical 404/not_found pairs.
Confirmed explicit public projection returned only display_name and id while excluding email, risk_score, and tenant_id.

Checked authorization-before-derived-output, explicit projection, private cache partition, precise-internal/generic-external reason, and rate-limit-not-confidentiality invariants across examples and answers.
invariant_checking.notes: The finite code does not model timing distributions, caches, external delivery, logs, infrastructure, or adaptive inference.

proof_review.notes: No formal noninterference, differential privacy, constant-time, statistical indistinguishability, serializer completeness, or authorization proof is claimed.

evidence: Confirmed the set-intersection statement is bounded by correctness of authorization sets and serializer, and explicitly excludes derived/side channels.
Confirmed response-equivalence testing is evidence against chosen distinguishers, never proof of universal noninterference.
Confirmed random IDs, 404, generic messages, random delay, GraphQL selection, rate limits, gateways, and public status are not presented as standalone confidentiality proofs.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Guarantees, heuristics, product tradeoffs, hypothetical examples, and production evidence obligations remain separate.

evidence: Snippet report artifacts/snippets/API-048/report.json records one passing deterministic local response/projection execution with five exact outputs.

Real serializer, database query, cache/CDN/gateway, timing distribution, delivery, rate-limit, logging, analytics, mixed-client, and penetration tests are required future evidence, not reported measurements.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production API, identity workflow, network timing study, CDN/cache, notification channel, or inference experiment was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed transcript-wide oracle modeling, explicit object/property/purpose projection, pre-derivation authorization, object existence policy, identity/recovery workflows, property/relationship minimization, GraphQL/batch/alternate paths, infrastructure/cache/compression, operational and side-effect data, statistical evidence, inference, and amplification as one coherent disclosure model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through action-specific response DTOs, authorized base queries, safe count/cursor/export semantics, generic account/private-object responses with protected internal reasons, dummy-hash/async recovery paths, field/edge resolver policy, cache partition/no-store, proxy-aware tests, privacy-safe rate controls, redacted telemetry, paired transcript suites, repeated timing distributions, and adaptive probe monitoring. Residual leakage and public discovery remain explicit product/risk decisions.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module expands from complete transcript modeling to projections, derived values, object/account equivalence, properties, GraphQL/batch, infrastructure, operations, and testing. Ten examples isolate login, object status, count, field, timing, GraphQL, batch, cache, analytics, and public-scraping cases; five exercises progress to physical access transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
